claims.feature: other: time compression in one sentence
claims.claim: Hobb advises skipping a dull stretch of travel by summarising it in one sentence, and supplies the sample sentence herself.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'What Works For Me', robinhobb.com blog, 2022
claims.quote: After four days of punishing travel, they reached a small holding
claims.page: Section: I don't want to write the next scene

claims.claim: Hobb says a chapter may consist of a single sentence.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'What Works For Me', robinhobb.com blog, 2022
claims.quote: You can have a one sentence chapter if you want
claims.page: Section: I don't want to write the next scene

claims.claim: Hobb rejects the word processor's thesaurus because it offers the same synonyms every other writer is using, and recommends a paper Roget's instead.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'What Works For Me', robinhobb.com blog, 2022
claims.quote: the same synonyms that every other writer is using

claims.claim: Hobb gives as a revision-pass example replacing a red car with candy apple red with metal flake.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, 'What Works For Me', robinhobb.com blog, 2022
claims.quote: The car isn't red, it's candy apple red with metal flake

claims.claim: Groell, the Random House editor of Hobb, Martin and others, says her first read of a book is close line-reading and individual sentence editing.
claims.source: Anne Groell, executive SFF editor, Random House USA, interviewed by Julie Crisp, 2016
claims.quote: I do the really close line-reading and individual sentence editing

claims.claim: Groell says she averages about 25 pages an hour, or 200 pages a day, on that first close read.
claims.source: Anne Groell, executive SFF editor, Random House USA, interviewed by Julie Crisp, 2016
claims.quote: I average about 25 pages an hour, or 200 pages a day

verdicts.trueWording: "You can just type, 'After four days of punishing travel...'"
verdicts.note: Raw page reached (robinhobb.com, HTTP 200). Section 'I don't want to write the next scene. It's boring.' Every limb holds: the boring stretch should not be written ('The solution. Don't write it.'), the four-day desert crossing is her own example, and she supplies the sentence verbatim - the page continues '...they reached a small holding near a water hole.' Or something similar.

verdicts.trueWording: "You can have a one sentence chapter if you want."
verdicts.note: Raw page reached. Exact sentence in the same section, immediately after the sample travel sentence, followed by 'It's your book.'

verdicts.trueWording: "the same synonyms that every other writer is using"
verdicts.note: Raw page reached. The asterisked footnote reads: 'Do you have a copy of Roget's Thesaurus? If not, go buy one now. A fat paper thesaurus is a treasure. See, if I look for a synonym for treasure via the word processing program I'm using, it will show me the same synonyms that every other writer is using. The thesaurus will give you a lot more choices.' Both limbs (rejection of the word-processor thesaurus, recommendation of a paper Roget's) are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: "The car isn't red, it's candy apple red with metal flake."
verdicts.note: Raw page reached. Section 'Nope. I'm blocked. Really blocked.' The 'revision-pass' limb is supported by the surrounding instruction: 'Go back four pages... Put on your editor hat and start looking at your work', with the car line as one of three sample line-edits.

verdicts.trueWording: "on my first read, I do the really close line-reading and individual sentence editing"

Martin through to Terry Brooks, Robin Hobb, Naomi Novik, Scott Lynch, Connie Willis' - note that framing is Crisp's, not Groell's own words.

verdicts.trueWording: "Going full out, I average about 25 pages an hour, or 200 pages a day"

One qualifier the claim drops: the page prefixes it with 'Going full out', and adds that an 800-pager therefore takes 4 solid days 'if there is nothing else to do - but there is always something else to do, meaning this often stretches to a week and a half.'
